column1: # tests/memfn/d3_floor.tsv -- THE D3 PCREC-ARTIFACT FLOOR's data (part_d.md §5.1 D3 [r3pd RDY-5]; R-43, R-44, d3fix), the ONE
# place its numbers live; d3_floor.py reads it, no number is a literal there. EVERY value is the MEASURED count of the
# gate's own sweep (d3fix, 2026-11-15, on 466d8e8ee's tree = d2496010e's compiler + the d3wire wiring; `make
# test-memfn-d3floor`, the D3-FLOOR lines), with a band ABOVE it: below the value = a loss (red), above value+band = a
# gain nobody re-pinned (red: "re-pin tests/memfn/d3_floor.tsv"), so a floor cannot go loose behind a growing census
# (review r10 D3W-1/2/5). To re-pin after a deliberate change: rerun the gate, read its D3-FLOOR lines, copy the numbers,
# say in the provenance column which change moved them.
# columns (tab-separated): cell, census_floor, census_band, compiles, failed, pop_band, records, records_band, provenance
#   census_floor  distinct corpus patterns whose SHIPPED art carries a run_part_terms record with an unspelled SET term.
#                 (r43 measured 58/143/99/216 on an earlier base; d3wire's census on d2496010e was 78/174/119/247 = these.)
#                 Must also be >= emit_sweep's live DIFFER_PINS floor for the cell (read there: the movers number has ONE home).
#   census_band   allowed gain over census_floor before the gate asks for a re-pin.
#   compiles      the POPULATION: corpus patterns that compiled (rc 0); fewer = a lost .rxt file / a crash wave; more than
#                 compiles+pop_band = the corpus grew, re-pin. failed = compiles that did not succeed (rc != 0 or timeout:
#                 deliberate rejects of the corpus, EXACT), so a crash wave names itself.
#   records       run_part_terms records on the shipped arts the sweep must see (a sweep whose summarize dropped the record
#                 again, p14, reds here too); records_band as pop_band.
